The most common security risk of intrusion through an access control system is by simply following a legitimate user through a door, referred to as "tailgating". Often, a legitimate user may hold the door for the intruder as an act of common courtesy. This risk can be minimized through security awareness training of the user population, or more active means such as turnstiles which admit only one person at a time.
